property_summary: After depositing X wei from caller A, A's recorded balance in c increases by exactly X (i.e., new_balance == old_balance + amt).
A zero-value call to Deposit must not revert and must leave the caller's balance unchanged while still adding a log entry (so call succeeds without reverting).
Calling Deposit with any amount should never revert (i.e., Deposit always accepts zero-value deposits).

Invariant: After any Deposit called by any account, the reference C always records the caller's increased balance in balances(msg.sender) (i.e. balances[msg.sender] >= deposited amount) even if the callee Log reverts or behaves adversarially; the mutant that removes the external Log call can change observable balances for other addresses when an adversarial reentrant Log contract is used, so a counterexample input (depositor, amount) exists that makes balances differ.

For any depositor and deposit amount, if the contract's Log file is a reentrant attacker that, when called from Deposit, reenters and performs a Collect that transfers funds out, then the reference C (which calls Log.AddMessage) preserves that such reentrancy cannot cause balances for ANY address to be lower than what a deposit by the same depositor just added; removing the Log call (mutant) can change balances observable after Deposit for some fuzzed depositor/amount and attacker behavior.

For every depositor and amount, if C's Log is set to a contract whose fallback/receive reenters and attempts to Collect, then in the correct contract the depositor's balance after Deposit is at least the deposited amount (the external Log call prevents reentrant funds-drain before balances update), whereas removing the Log call (mutant) allows a reentrant attacker to drain funds so this rule can be violated for some fuzzed depositor/amount.
